question: Why did attention and the transformer replace RNN seq2seq models, and how is a transformer trained, inspected, fine-tuned and distilled?

limits: No datasets sizes, accuracy numbers or hyperparameter study given; fine-tuning and distillation demos are shown only as confusion matrices (Figs 2.25, 2.29).

Chapter errors against Vaswani et al.: scales by square root of D described as 'size of the sequence'; cross-attention says queries come from the encoder; 'QT' typo for LM; says Google researchers 'in 2016' for Attention Is All You Need (2017).
Claims that decoder-only models dominate generative AI and that BERT-like text generation appeared in 2024 are stated without data.
practices: Use subword tokenisation (BPE) to avoid <UNK> tokens (Training a transformer, p.19-20).
Prefer sampling (top-k, top-p, temperature) over greedy decoding for generation (p.18-19).
For classification fine-tuning, freeze most layers and train one or two added layers on top, with a very low learning rate if unfreezing (p.29-30).
Use knowledge distillation (KL divergence between teacher and student logits, teacher in inference only) when compute is the limit (p.34-36).
Use NMF rather than PCA to inspect FFN activations because it avoids negative activations (p.27).
Mask the upper triangle with -inf in decoder self-attention to prevent seeing the future (p.15).
